name: Robotic Total Abdominal Colectomy
overview: Robot-assisted complete colectomy with ileorectal anastomosis

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the operative advantage of robotic total colectomy over laparoscopic?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Multi-quadrant dissection with a single docking (newer Xi platform rotates arms), enhanced 3D visualization for splenic/hepatic flexure mobilization, and reduced conversion rates in obese patients. The Si platform required re-docking; the Xi platform operates across all quadrants.

pimpingQuestions.question: What vascular pedicles are divided during robotic total colectomy?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Ileocolic, right colic (if present), middle colic (right and left branches), and IMA. All from the SMA/IMA system. The marginal artery is entirely removed with the specimen. Both ureters must be identified before pedicle ligation.

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the anastomosis after robotic total colectomy?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Ileorectal anastomosis (IRA) -- typically side-to-end stapled or hand-sewn. The rectum is divided at the sacral promontory. The ileal-rectal anastomosis heals well due to the ileum's robust SMA blood supply and the rectum's middle/inferior rectal arteries.

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the indication for total colectomy in FAP versus Lynch syndrome?
pimpingQuestions.answer: FAP: total proctocolectomy with IPAA (entire colon and rectum at cancer risk). Lynch syndrome: total colectomy with IRA (rectum can be surveilled, lower morbidity). The distinction matters because FAP has near-100% rectal cancer risk while Lynch has lower rectal involvement.

pimpingQuestions.question: What functional outcome difference exists between IRA and IPAA?
pimpingQuestions.answer: IRA: 3-5 stools/day (better function, rectum provides reservoir). IPAA: 5-8 stools/day (no rectal reservoir, but eliminates rectal cancer risk). IRA patients need lifelong rectal surveillance with annual proctoscopy for new polyps/cancer.
